entities.summary: Agostino di Duccio was a renowned Italian sculptor of the early Renaissance, born in unknown circumstances and active in the 15th century. He is best known for his work in the Siena Cathedral, where he created several notable sculptures, including the famous 'Majesties of the Baptistery' series. Di Duccio's innovative use of perspective and his ability to capture the human form in marble helped to redefine the art of sculpture in Italy and paved the way for future generations of artists. His legacy can be seen in the works of artists such as Donatello and Michelangelo, who were heavily influenced by his techniques and style. Despite his significant contributions to the art world, di Duccio's life remains somewhat of a mystery, with little information available about his early years or personal life. Nonetheless, his impact on the development of Renaissance art is undeniable, and his work continues to be celebrated and studied by art historians and enthusiasts alike.
